Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: History of occasional anxiety/panic; atopic background (eczema).
- Precipitating factors: Acute stressor (wasp/bee sting) with concern about anaphylaxis.
- Perpetuating factors: Health-related worry and catastrophic interpretation of bodily sensations (subjective dyspnea/lip sensations) despite normal observed breathing and exam.
- Protective factors: Insightful help-seeking, stable employment, pet companionship.
DDx alignment: Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea (hyperventilation component) is plausible in context of a localized sting reaction without objective airway compromise.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce anxiety during/after similar health incidents; understand warning signs requiring urgent care; feel confident managing symptoms.
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide targeted psychoeducation and brief anxiety management strategies; monitor for recurrence or escalation; screen for anxiety/panic disorder if symptoms persist.
- Actions (Patient): 
  - Review provided information on anaphylaxis warning signs and follow emergency guidance if they occur.
  - Monitor anxiety triggers/symptoms related to health scares; note frequency, intensity, duration.
  - Seek follow-up if anxiety episodes recur or impair functioning.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Reinforce psychoeducation on differentiating normal localized reactions vs emergencies.
  - At follow-up, screen for anxiety/panic disorder if episodes persist (e.g., standardized screening; consider brief CBT/self-help resources if indicated).
  - Safety-netting: clear instructions for urgent escalation (A&E) if red flags develop.

Secondary Problem (if applicable): History of occasional panic/anxiety episodes
- Patient Goal(s): Clarify whether these represent panic attacks; reduce episode frequency.
- Clinical Goal(s): Determine diagnosis (if any); develop management plan if clinically significant (e.g., psychoeducation, brief CBT; medications only if indicated).
- Actions (Patient): Keep a brief symptom diary (triggers, physical sensations, thoughts, behaviors).
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange dedicated mental health review if episodes continue; consider referral options if clinically warranted (psychological therapies). No referrals initiated in this visit.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Normal localized reactions vs. signs of anaphylaxis (lip/tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, stridor), when to seek urgent care; use of antihistamines.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing dyspnea, audible stridor, progressive lip/tongue swelling, voice change, widespread hives, dizziness/syncope.
- Coping Strategies: Not recorded.
